messages.text: The files describe three CRM users, Google Workspace, and a $180/month budget with a preference for monthly billing. The key requirement is preserving firms, their locations, and contacts shared across locations—including when you export notes and quotes. I’m checking that alongside pricing.

Three seats; target maximum USD 180/month total, month-to-month preferred. Google Workspace email, shared spreadsheets and PDF quotes; three people handle sales. We need a usable inbox/activity history, follow-up ownership, organization/contact relationships, CSV import, and an exit path that includes notes and attached quotes. No sales automation or bulk sending is required to start.

The sales notes mention firms with several locations and contacts shared across locations. Do locations need their own lasting records, or would a location field on each sales opportunity be enough?
- Keep separate location records and shared-contact links

messages.text: One important difference has emerged: some affordable plans handle deals well but restrict custom relationships between records. Attio’s custom relationships require Pro, which exceeds your budget. Zoho offers more flexibility, but its documented CSV import limitation for multi-select relationships needs a close look.

Zoho CRM Enterprise is my current first choice to trial at $150/month for three seats, because its relationship fields fit firms, locations, and shared contacts. A newer Zoho import guide supports those links, despite an older page saying otherwise, so the trial should verify the importer available in your account. I’m preparing a comparison and a small test using your sample pipeline.

The built-in browser is unavailable here, so I can verify public documentation but can’t test the CRM interfaces.

Organizations, locations, contacts, notes and attached quotes must survive migration and an eventual export. A property management firm can own several locations, and a contact may work for more than one location. Losing that relationship during import or export would be expensive.
